title: DISTINCT that only removes the duplicates a join created
prompt: Weekly 'customers active on a channel' extract. For @Channel = 'Web' over one year the join produces about 2.7M rows
and a Hash Match (Distinct) reduces them to about 610k customers. Runtime about 22 s, with a 900 MB memory grant and
a spill on busy nights. The output must have one row per customer: the next step loads it into a table whose primary
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Customers: 2.0M rows. Tier S = 1.85M, G = ~150k, P = 25 partner accounts (CustomerID 1 to 25). IsActive = 1 for 88%. Email is NULL for ~9% (~180k rows, ~160k of them active). About 2% of non-NULL emails are shared by two or more customer rows (households). ReferredByCustomerID is non-NULL for 18%; 312 rows are self-referrals (ReferredByCustomerID = CustomerID, CustomerID 500001 to 500312). AccountNumber always matches 'AC' + 10 digits (CHECK constraint).

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.
baseline_sql: JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

correct_families.description: A semi join returns each customer once. The select list holds the primary key, so no DISTINCT is needed.
IN over the customers that have a qualifying order is the same semi join.

traps.why: Removing DISTINCT while the join stays returns one row per order: a customer with 12 orders appears 12 times and the load fails on the primary key.
traps.told_apart_by: Any customer with two qualifying orders.
example_sql: JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

traps.why: A semi join that keeps only the date predicate returns customers who ordered on another channel.
traps.told_apart_by: A customer whose only orders since @From are Store orders, with @Channel = 'Web'.

min_improvement.basis: Provisional: no reference measurement. The distinct over 2.7M joined rows and its spill must go.

key.reference_notes: Contrast with the task converted from rewrite exam Q14, where the output column is not a key and DISTINCT must stay.
